This just suddenly occurred to me. The gig economy is the most pragmatic and natural transition to libertarian socialism since unions formed a century ago. It's a peaceful approach to worker owned means of production. I believe we just have to keep the old gate keepers out of the way.

This is really just going to be a matter of time, coding and will power, but it's totally feasible to form a strong co-op based on direct democracy and free association. It's not just possible, but likely. Removing the overhead from the barrier of entry into the market place seems necessary.

This is what I'm envisioning. There could be an open source app, that connects local producers to urban consumers. Professional drivers could make deliveries from shops, chefs, etc, during the day and drive party people home at night. There could be mechanics, barbers, doctors, etc that make house calls. There could be time banks. There could be a tool share program, where you rent out tools that you're not using. There could be instructor owned workshops. There could be print shops run from home. And there could be crowd lending for ambitious projects. There could be real estate buy ins for housing co-ops. There could be user owned liability and health insurance with democratic management.

The truth is that this shit won't be right for everybody, because nothing is for everybody. There will be very little job security. But there will be freedom. You might have to work a few short hour jobs to get ahead. But you won't have a boss.
